info.title: Orvano
info.description: The Orvano API. Every path lives under /v1.

post.description: Signs a new user up with an email and password, and signs them in.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

get.description: Gets the signed in user. A server can call it with a user's access token to check that the session is still active.

patch.description: Changes the signed in user's name or metadata.

post.description: Deletes the signed in user with all their sessions. It can't be undone.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

put.description:
Starts changing the signed in user's email: emails a confirmation link to the new address. The email changes
when that link is opened.

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

post.description:
Emails a 6 digit sign in code that works for 10 minutes. An email without a user gets one that creates the user,
unless `createUser` is false. The answer is the same 202 either way.

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

post.description:
Changes a user's email to the new address with the token from the confirmation link, and marks it verified. It
needs no session and keeps every session. The token works once.

get.description: Lists the signed in user's identities, oldest first.

post.description:
Links a provider to the signed in user with its ID token from a native app. Needs the user's current password when
they have one (or a second factor on this session within 10 minutes); a user without a password needs a session at
most 10 minutes old.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

post.description: Links the provider with the code a link flow returned and its verifier. Only the user who started the flow can finish it.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

post.description:
Starts linking a provider to the signed in user, like `createOAuthFlow`. Needs the user's current password when
they have one (or a second factor on this session within 10 minutes); a user without a password needs a session at
most 10 minutes old. The SDKs' `linkIdentity` does all of it.

delete.description: Unlinks one of the signed in user's identities. The last way to sign in can't be removed. Sessions stay.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description:
Emails a sign in link. An email without a user gets one that creates the user, unless `createUser` is false. The
answer is the same 202 either way, so it never tells anyone which emails have accounts.

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

get.description: Gets the signed in user's MFA state.

post.description:
Starts a step up with a passkey: answers the options for `navigator.credentials.get`, listing the signed in user's
passkeys. Send the passkey's answer to `account.verifyMfa`.

Replaces the user's recovery codes with 10 new ones; every older code stops working. Needs MFA on and a second
factor on this session within 10 minutes (`account.verifyMfa`).

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

post.description:
Starts turning on an authenticator app: answers a new secret, replacing any that still waits for its first code.
Needs the user's current password when they have one (or a second factor on this session within 10 minutes; a
user without a password needs a session that signed in within 10 minutes) and, when the user has an email, a
verified one.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

delete.description:
Turns MFA off: removes the authenticator app and every recovery code. Sessions stay. Needs a second factor on this
session within 10 minutes (`account.verifyMfa`).

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description:
Turns MFA on with the first code from the authenticator app, within 15 minutes of `account.createTotp`. Answers 10
new recovery codes, ends every other session of the user, and raises this one to level 2 with a new access token.
The SDKs keep their stored refresh token, whose next refresh carries `aal` 2 too.

Step up: checks a second factor on the signed in session, so security changes work for the next 10 minutes. Raises
the session to level 2 and answers a new access token; the refresh token is not sent and stays unchanged. The SDK
helpers (`verifyMfa`) store the access token.

Starts signing in with a provider: answers the provider's sign in page to send the browser to. After the user
agrees, Orvano sends the browser back to `redirectUrl` with a code that only your verifier redeems. The SDKs'
`signInWithOAuth` does all of it.
Finishes adding a passkey with the browser's or the platform's answer to `account.createPasskeyRegistration`.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

get.description: Lists the signed in user's passkeys, oldest first, including inactive ones.

post.description:
Starts adding a passkey: answers the options for `navigator.credentials.create`. Needs passkeys turned on, the
user's current password when they have one (or a second factor on this session within 10 minutes; a user without a
password needs a session that signed in within 10 minutes), a verified email when the user has one, and fewer than
10 passkeys.

patch.description: Renames one of the signed in user's passkeys.

delete.description:
Removes one of the signed in user's passkeys. A user with MFA on needs a second factor on this session within 10
minutes (`account.verifyMfa`); a user without it needs a session that signed in within 10 minutes.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

put.description: Changes the signed in user's password and ends every other session of theirs.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description:
Emails a password reset link, if the email belongs to an active user. The answer is the same 202 whether or not
it does, so it never tells anyone which emails have accounts.

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

post.description:
Sets a new password with the token from a reset link, and signs the user in. Every other session of the user
ends, and the email counts as verified. The token works once.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

get.description: Lists the signed in user's active sessions, newest first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Sessions per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

delete.description: Ends every session of the signed in user except the current one.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

delete.description: Signs out: ends the current session.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description: Signs a user in with an emailed code. After 5 wrong tries the code stops working; ask for a new one.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

post.description:
Signs a user in with a provider's ID token from a native app (Google or Apple sign in), and with Apple's
authorization code. It finds the user by the provider account, else by the provider's verified email, else
creates them. Each token works once.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

post.description: Signs a user in with the token from a magic link, creating them when the link was for a new email. The token works once.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

post.description:
Finishes a sign in that answered an MFA challenge: checks the ticket and one factor, then creates the session.
After 5 wrong factors the ticket stops working; sign in again.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

post.description:
Starts answering an MFA challenge with a passkey: answers the options for `navigator.credentials.get`, listing the
user's passkeys. Send the passkey's answer to `account.createMfaSession`. Never counts as a wrong attempt.

Signs a user in with the code a provider flow returned and the flow's PKCE verifier. It finds the user by the
provider account, else by the provider's verified email, else creates them. The code works once.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

post.description:
Signs in with a passkey's answer to `account.createPasskeyChallenge`. A passkey counts as two factors, so this sign
in is never asked for MFA and the session starts at level 2.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

post.description:
Starts a passkey sign in: answers a challenge with an empty `allowCredentials`, so the browser or the platform
offers every passkey of the RP ID, including through autofill. Needs passkeys turned on for the project.
Signs a user in with their email and password.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

post.description: Trades the current refresh token for a new pair. The old token keeps answering with the same pair for 10 seconds, so a retry is safe.

delete.description: Ends one of the signed in user's sessions.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description: Emails the signed in user a link that verifies their email.

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

post.description:
Verifies a user's email with the token from a verification link. It needs no session and creates none; a client
signed in as that user refreshes its session, so the access token's claim changes at once. The token works once.

get.description: Checks that the server is up and returns its version.
Gets a project's public signing keys, to check its access tokens.
Gets a project's discovery document, for JWT libraries that configure themselves from the issuer.
Lists the project's users, newest first.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Only users whose email starts with this, ignoring case.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only users with this status: `active` or `blocked`.

parameters.name: createdAfter
parameters.description: Only users created after this time.

parameters.name: createdBefore
parameters.description: Only users created before this time.

parameters.name: emailVerified
parameters.description: Only verified users (true) or unverified users (false).

parameters.name: mfa
parameters.description: Only users with MFA `on` or `off`. With the project's authenticator app switch off, every user counts as `off`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Users per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

post.description: Creates a user with an email and password. It does not sign them in.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

delete.description: Deletes a user with their password and sessions. It can't be undone.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description: Blocks a user: ends every session and refuses sign in. Blocking a blocked user changes nothing.

put.description:
Changes a user's email at once, without a confirmation email. It deletes the user's live email links and codes,
and keeps their sessions.
Marks a user's email verified or unverified. Marking it verified deletes any live verification links.

get.description: Lists a user's identities, oldest first.

delete.description: Unlinks one of a user's identities. The user's last way to sign in can't be removed. Sessions stay.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

get.description: A user's MFA state: whether sign in asks them for a second factor, their recovery codes left, and their passkeys.

post.description:
Turns MFA off for a user who lost every factor: deletes their authenticator app and recovery codes and ends all
their sessions. Their passkeys stay. A user without MFA is left as they are.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

get.description: Lists a user's passkeys, oldest first, including inactive ones.

delete.description: Removes one of a user's passkeys. Sessions stay.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description: Emails a user a password reset link.

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

get.description: Lists a user's active sessions, newest first. `current` is always false.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Sessions per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

delete.description: Ends every session of a user.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

delete.description: Ends one session of a user.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description: Unblocks a user so they can sign in again. Their old sessions stay ended.
Emails a user a link that verifies their email.

user.description: The user; null while `mfa` is set.

session.description: The new session's tokens; null while `mfa` is set.

mfa.description:
Set when the user has MFA on: no session exists yet. Finish with `account.createMfaSession` and the ticket before
it expires. The SDKs' `completeMfa` does it. Null otherwise.

isNewUser.description: Whether this call created the user: true from sign up, from a magic link or email code for a new email, and from a provider sign in that created the user.

verificationEmail.description: What happened to the verification email sign up was asked to send; null when none was asked for.

AuthResult.description:
A signed in user and their new session, or, for a user with MFA on, the challenge to answer first. Exactly one of
`session` and `mfa` is set.

code.description: The `orvano_code` parameter Orvano added to your redirect URL. It works once, for 2 minutes.

codeVerifier.description: The PKCE verifier whose challenge started the link flow.

CompleteOAuthLinkRequest.description: A link of a provider to the signed in user, with the code a link flow returned.

credential.description: The browser's or the platform's answer.

name.description: 1 to 64 characters. Left out, the passkey is named `Passkey`.

token.description: The `orvano_token` parameter of the emailed link.

password.description: The new password: 8 to 256 characters after Unicode NFKC normalization.

CompleteRecoveryRequest.description: A password reset, with the token from the emailed link.

token.description: The `orvano_token` parameter of the emailed link.

ConfirmEmailChangeRequest.description: An email change confirmation, with the token from the link sent to the new address.

code.description: The 6 digit code the authenticator app shows now.

ConfirmTotpRequest.description: The first code from the authenticator app, which turns MFA on.

email.description: The email, trimmed, at most 320 characters. Unique in the project, ignoring case.

password.description: 8 to 256 characters after Unicode NFKC normalization.

name.description: A display name, at most 256 characters.

verificationRedirectUrl.description:
When set, also emails a verification link that opens here: a host that is one of the project's web platforms, or
your app's own scheme. `AuthResult.verificationEmail` says whether it was sent.

CreateAccountRequest.description: A new user with an email and password.

createUser.description: Whether the code may create a user for an email that has none. Defaults to true.

CreateEmailCodeSessionRequest.description: A sign in with an emailed code.

provider.description: The provider that issued the token.

idToken.description: The provider's ID token, at most 8 KB.

nonce.description:
The raw nonce, 16 to 128 characters. Give the provider its lowercase hex SHA-256 (the SDKs' `createNonce` makes

authorizationCode.description: Apple only, and required for Apple: the authorization code Sign in with Apple returned with the token.

name.description: Apple only: the name Sign in with Apple returned on the first authorization, at most 256 characters.

password.description:
The user's current password. A user who has one sends it, unless this session passed a second factor within 10

CreateIdTokenIdentityRequest.description: A link of a provider to the signed in user with its ID token from a native app.

provider.description: The provider that issued the token.

idToken.description: The provider's ID token, at most 8 KB.

nonce.description:
The raw nonce, 16 to 128 characters. Give the provider its lowercase hex SHA-256 (the SDKs' `createNonce` makes
both), so the token carries that hash.

authorizationCode.description: Apple only, and required for Apple: the authorization code Sign in with Apple returned with the token.

name.description: Apple only: the name Sign in with Apple returned on the first authorization, at most 256 characters.

CreateIdTokenSessionRequest.description: A sign in with a provider's ID token from a native app.

email.description: The email to sign in as; case does not matter.

token.description: The `orvano_token` parameter of the emailed link.

totpCode.description: The 6 digit code the authenticator app shows now.

recoveryCode.description: A recovery code; case, spaces, and hyphens do not matter. Each works once.

Your page or app that receives the result: a host that is one of the project's web platforms (`http` only on

The S256 PKCE challenge: base64url(SHA-256(verifier)), 43 characters. Keep the verifier; only it redeems the

password.description:

credential.description: The browser's or the platform's answer.

email.description: The email the user signed up with; case does not matter.

CreatePasswordSessionRequest.description: A sign in with an email and password.

email.description: The email of the account; case does not matter.

CreateRecoveryRequest.description: A request to email a password reset link.

password.description:

minutes. A user without one leaves it out, and must have signed in within 10 minutes.

email.description: The email, trimmed, at most 320 characters. Unique in the project, ignoring case.

password.description: 8 to 256 characters after Unicode NFKC normalization.

name.description: A display name, at most 256 characters.

emailVerified.description: True to create the user with their email already verified, as when importing accounts. Defaults to false.

CreateUserRequest.description: A new user with an email and password, created by a server. No session is created.

redirectUrl.description:
The page that receives the link: a host that is one of the project's web platforms (`http` only on `localhost` or
`127.0.0.1`), or the app's own scheme. The link adds `orvano_type=verification` and `orvano_token` to it.

CreateUserVerificationRequest.description: A request to email a user a link that verifies their email.

redirectUrl.description:
Your page that receives the link: a host that is one of the project's web platforms (`http` only on `localhost`
or `127.0.0.1`), or your app's own scheme (its iOS, Android, or macOS identifier). The link adds
`orvano_type=verification` and `orvano_token` to it.

CreateVerificationRequest.description: A request to email a verification link to the signed in user.

password.description: The user's current password. A user without one leaves it out, and must have signed in within 10 minutes.

DeleteAccountRequest.description: A request to delete the signed in user.

EmailLinkType.description:
What an emailed link is for: the `orvano_type` parameter Orvano adds to every link it emails, beside
`orvano_token`. The SDKs' link helpers (`redeemLink`, `handleLink`) read it to call the right operation.

ErrorCode.description: Every stable error code the server sends in `Problem.code`.

Health.description: Whether the server is up, and which Orvano version it runs.

IdTokenProvider.description: A provider a native app can sign in with by its ID token.

subject.description: The provider's ID for the account: Google's and Apple's `sub`, GitHub's user ID, Microsoft's `<tid>:<oid>`.

email.description: The email the provider gave, verified or not; null when it gave none.

emailVerified.description: Whether the provider vouches for that email.

lastSignInAt.description: When the user last signed in with it; null if never.

Identity.description: A provider account linked to a user: one way the user signs in.

IdentityList.description: A user's identities, oldest first: at most one per provider.

x.description: The public point's x coordinate, base64url.

y.description: The public point's y coordinate, base64url.

kid.description: The key ID, the `kid` in a token's header.

Jwk.description: One public signing key, as a JSON Web Key (RFC 7517).

Jwks.description: A project's public signing keys: the active key and any key retired within the last 24 hours.

ticket.description:
Proves the first step passed; send it to `account.createMfaSession`. Keep it in memory only. Empty when the ticket
travels in a cookie instead (the console).

factors.description: The factors the user can answer with now, in this order: `totp`, `recovery_code`, `passkey`.

expiresAt.description: When the ticket stops working: 5 minutes after the first step. After that, sign in again.

MfaChallenge.description:
The second step a sign in must pass before it gets a session: the user has MFA on. Answer it with
`account.createMfaSession` before `expiresAt`.

mfaEnabled.description: Whether sign in asks for a second factor: a confirmed authenticator app, while the project allows TOTP.

totpConfirmed.description: Whether an authenticator app is confirmed, even while the project has TOTP turned off.

totpConfirmedAt.description: When the authenticator app was confirmed; null when none is.

recoveryCodesRemaining.description: How many unused recovery codes are left, 0 to 10.

passkeyCount.description: How many of the user's passkeys can sign in now.

factorsAvailable.description: What the project lets users turn on now: `totp` and `passkey`.

url.description: Send the browser here: the provider's sign in page.

OAuthLinkType.description:
What a provider redirect came back for: the `orvano_type` parameter Orvano adds when it sends the browser back to
your `redirectUrl`, beside `orvano_code` or `orvano_error`. The SDKs' link helpers read it.

issuer.description: The issuer, the `iss` of every access token of the project.

OpenIdConfiguration.description:
The discovery document standard JWT libraries configure themselves from. Orvano is not an OpenID provider;
this exists so tools that take an issuer URL find the keys. Its names are the standard snake case ones.

name.description: The name the user gave it, else `Passkey`.

lastUsedAt.description: When it last signed in or answered a challenge; null when it never has.

synced.description: Whether the passkey is backed up and synced across devices (for example by iCloud Keychain or a password manager).

active.description: Whether it can sign in now: false after the project's RP ID changed away from the one it was made for.

credential.description: The browser's or the platform's answer.

PasskeyAnswer.description: A passkey's answer to a challenge.

rawId.description: The credential ID again, base64url; must equal `id`.

authenticatorAttachment.description: `platform` or `cross-platform`; null when the browser does not say.

PasskeyAssertionCredential.description: A passkey's answer in WebAuthn's JSON form: what `PublicKeyCredential.toJSON()` gives after `get`.

userHandle.description: The user handle the passkey stores, base64url; null when the authenticator gives none.

transports.description: How the authenticator was reached: `internal`, `hybrid`, `usb`, `nfc`, or `ble`.

residentKey.description: Always `required`: the passkey is discoverable, so it signs in with no email typed.

PasskeyAuthenticatorSelection.description: What kind of authenticator a new passkey must come from.

challengeId.description: Names this challenge; send it back with the answer within 5 minutes.

PasskeyChallenge.description: A challenge for a passkey to sign: pass `options` to the browser, then send its answer with `challengeId`.

user.description: The user the passkey is for.

pubKeyCredParams.description: The key types the server accepts, in order of preference.

timeout.description: How long the browser waits, in milliseconds: 300000.

excludeCredentials.description: The user's passkeys under this RP ID, so the same authenticator is not registered twice.

attestation.description: Always `none`: no device certificate is asked for.

PasskeyCreationOptions.description:
The options for `navigator.credentials.create` in WebAuthn's JSON form. Pass them to
`PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON`, or let the SDK's `registerPasskey` do it.

transports.description: How the authenticator was reached when the passkey was made: `internal`, `hybrid`, `usb`, `nfc`, or `ble`.

PasskeyCredentialDescriptor.description: One passkey, named by its credential ID.

PasskeyCredentialParameters.description: A key type the server accepts.

PasskeyList.description: A user's passkeys, oldest first; at most 10.

challengeId.description: Names this registration; send it back with the new passkey within 5 minutes.

PasskeyRegistration.description: A started passkey registration: pass `options` to the browser, then send its answer with `challengeId`.

rawId.description: The credential ID again, base64url; must equal `id`.

authenticatorAttachment.description: `platform` or `cross-platform`; null when the browser does not say.

PasskeyRegistrationCredential.description: A new passkey in WebAuthn's JSON form: what `PublicKeyCredential.toJSON()` gives after `create`.

id.description: The RP ID: the domain passkeys are bound to.

name.description: The name an authenticator shows: the project's RP name, else the project name.

PasskeyRelyingParty.description: The relying party of a passkey: the app's passkey domain and the name people see.

timeout.description: How long the browser waits, in milliseconds: 300000.

allowCredentials.description: The passkeys that may answer; empty for sign in, so the browser offers every passkey for the RP ID.

PasskeyRequestOptions.description:
The options for `navigator.credentials.get` in WebAuthn's JSON form. Pass them to
`PublicKeyCredential.parseRequestOptionsFromJSON`, or let the SDK's helpers do it.

id.description: The user handle: the user ID's 16 bytes, base64url.

name.description: The user's email, else their user ID.

displayName.description: The user's name, else their email, else `User`.

PasskeyUserEntity.description: The account a new passkey is for, as the authenticator stores it.

title.description: The standard HTTP reason phrase for the status.

detail.description: A short, safe sentence about this occurrence, when the server has one.

code.description: Orvano's stable error code, from the `ErrorCode` catalog. SDKs treat it as a plain string.

requestId.description: The request ID to quote when reporting a problem; also sent as `X-Request-Id`.

Problem.description:
An RFC 9457 problem details body. Every operation declares it as its `default` response, sent
as `application/problem+json`.

accessToken.description: An ES256 JWT, valid for 15 minutes.

sessionId.description: The session ID, also the `sid` claim of the access token.

RaisedSession.description:
The signed in session after a second factor: a new access token carrying the new `aal` and `amr` claims. The refresh
token is not sent; keep the one you hold, which is unchanged and whose next refresh carries the new claims too.

codes.description: 10 recovery codes, each `XXXXX-XXXXX`, each working once.

RecoveryCodes.description: New recovery codes. Show them once and ask the user to keep them safe; every older code stopped working.

RefreshSessionRequest.description: A trade of a refresh token for a new pair.

lastRefreshedAt.description: When the session last traded its refresh token.

userAgent.description: The user agent that signed in, at most 512 characters; null when none was sent.

sdk.description: The SDK that signed in, from `X-Orvano-SDK`; null when none was sent.

ipAddress.description: The IP address last seen for the session; null when unknown.

current.description: Whether this is the session making the call.

provider.description: The provider of an `oauth` or `id_token` session; null for every other method.

aal.description:
How strongly the session signed in: 1 for one factor, 2 once a second factor or a passkey was verified on it. Also
the access token's `aal` claim.

amr.description:
The ways the user proved who they are on this session, sorted: `pwd`, `email`, `fed`, `otp`, `rec`, `hwk`, `swk`,
`user`, and `mfa` (whenever `aal` is 2). Also the access token's `amr` claim.

Session.description: An active session of a user: one signed in device or browser.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` to get the next page; null on the last page.

SessionPage.description: One page of a user's active sessions, newest first.

accessToken.description: An ES256 JWT, valid for 15 minutes.

refreshToken.description: Trades itself for a new pair once; keep it secret.

refreshTokenExpiresAt.description: When the session ends unless it refreshes first: 30 days idle, or 365 days after sign in.

sessionId.description: The session ID, also the `sid` claim of the access token.

SessionTokens.description:
A session's tokens. Send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer`; trade the refresh token for a new pair
before the access token expires. The SDKs do both for you.

recoveryCodes.description: 10 recovery codes, each `XXXXX-XXXXX`, each working once.

session.description: A new access token for this session, carrying `aal` 2. Keep the refresh token you hold; it is unchanged.

TotpConfirmation.description:
MFA is on. Show the recovery codes once and ask the user to keep them safe; they can't be read again. Every other
session of the user has ended, and this one is now at level 2.

secret.description: The secret: 20 random bytes as unpadded base32 (32 characters). Never log it.

uri.description: The `otpauth://` URI an authenticator app scans: the project as the issuer, the user's email as the label.

expiresAt.description: When the secret stops waiting for its first code; ask for a new one after that.

TotpSetup.description:
A new authenticator app secret, waiting for its first code. Show `uri` as a QR code and `secret` for typing in, then
confirm with `account.confirmTotp` within 15 minutes.

name.description: A new display name of at most 256 characters, or null to remove it.

metadata.description: New metadata, replacing the old: a JSON object of at most 16 KB.

UpdateAccountRequest.description: Changes to the signed in user. A field left out stays as it is.

email.description: The new email, trimmed, at most 320 characters.

redirectUrl.description:
Your page that receives the confirmation link: a host that is one of the project's web platforms, or your app's
own scheme. The link adds `orvano_type=email_change` and `orvano_token` to it.

password.description: The user's current password. A user without one leaves it out, and must have signed in within 10 minutes.

UpdateEmailRequest.description: A request to change the signed in user's email. It changes once the link sent to the new address is opened.

verified.description: True marks it verified (keeping an earlier date); false marks it unverified.

UpdateEmailVerificationRequest.description: Sets whether a user's email is verified.

UpdatePasskeyRequest.description: A new name for a passkey.

currentPassword.description: The user's current password. A user without one leaves it out, and must have signed in within 10 minutes.

newPassword.description: The new password: 8 to 256 characters after Unicode NFKC normalization.

email.description: The new email, trimmed, at most 320 characters. Unique in the project, ignoring case.

emailVerified.description: True marks the new email verified; it is unverified otherwise. Defaults to false.

UpdateUserEmailRequest.description: Changes a user's email at once, without a confirmation email.

email.description: The email, as typed at sign up; null for a user without one.

emailVerified.description: Whether the email has been verified. Also the access token's `email_verified` claim.

emailVerifiedAt.description: When the email was verified; null while it is not.

name.description: The display name; null when none was given.

status.description: Whether the user may sign in.

metadata.description: Your own data about the user: a JSON object of at most 16 KB.

lastSignInAt.description: When the user last signed in; null if never.

providers.description: The providers linked to the user, sorted by name.

hasPassword.description: Whether the user has a password.

mfaEnabled.description:
Whether MFA is on: the user has confirmed an authenticator app and the project allows it. A passkey alone never
turns it on.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` to get the next page; null on the last page.

UserPage.description: One page of a project's users, newest first.

UserStatus.description: Whether a user may sign in.

VerificationEmailStatus.description: What happened to the verification email of a sign up. The user and session are created whatever it says.

token.description: The `orvano_token` parameter of the emailed link.

VerifyEmailRequest.description: An email verification, with the token from the emailed link.

totpCode.description: The 6 digit code the authenticator app shows now.

recoveryCode.description: A recovery code; case, spaces, and hyphens do not matter. Each works once.

VerifyMfaRequest.description: A second factor for a step up: exactly one of the fields.

consoleSession.name: orvano_console
consoleSession.description:
A console account's session: the `orvano_console` cookie (`HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`), set by
`consoleAccount.create`, `consoleAccount.createSession` (when the account has no MFA), and the second step and
passkey sign in that finish it. Browsers send it themselves.

bearer.description: A signed in user's access token: `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`, an ES256 JWT.

apiKey.name: X-Orvano-Key
apiKey.description: A server's API key: `X-Orvano-Key: orv_sk_...`, holding the scopes the operation needs.
